newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay outlines move to new HK airport.
newsitem.headline: Cathay outlines move to new HK airport.

text.p: The relocation strategy for the move to Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok (CLK) airport by Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd is intended to ensure revenue-producing flight schedules and business continuity are maintained, the airline's in-house newspaper said.
Gary Gibb, Cathay's liaison and planning manager, said the move will be in 12 phases starting early next year and will continue until April 1999. The airport is scheduled to open in April next year.

The airline's 4,900 million Hong Kong dollars (U.S.$632.9 million) "Cathay Pacific City" headquarters now taking shape at CLK will house more than 4,000 staff under one roof for the first time. The one million sq ft building includes a 350 room hotel for flight crew and a dedicated training centre.
The first staff to switch will be members of the airline's operations department who will move to CLK's passenger terminal to support the transfer of flight operations.
The night before the airport opens, all aircraft at the existing Kai Tak airport will be ferried to the new airport along with ground handling equipment ready for the first day's business.
Most airline equipment will be transported by road although container barges are available as a fall-back solution, the newspaper said.
